newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher on reports India buys wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher on reports India buys wheat.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures ended higher on Wednesday, boosted by widespread reports that India bought one million tonnes of Australian wheat and talk more business was in the works, traders said.

U.S. and European exporters and traders said India bought one million tonnes of Australian wheat. However, officials at the Australian embassy in Washington and the Australian Wheat Board in New York could not confirm the deal.
Floor sources and exporters said India may be in the market for more wheat for delivery before the monsoon season begins later this year.
Commercials were conspicuous buyers on the day but several traders said the moves were to cover existing positions rather than establish new ones.
"The commercials are a little nervous about going into the (USDA) report short," a floor trader said.
Analysts expected Monday's USDA prospective plantings report to show all U.S. wheat plantings at 70.10 million acres, down more than five million from last year's figure of 75.64 million acres.
Wheat closed five to 10 cents per bushel higher with May up six at $3.95-1/2 a bushel.
New crop months were also supported by lingering concerns that unfavorable weather in all three key U.S. wheat growing regions would further cut production.

Floor sources cited persistent dry weather in the hard red winter wheat growing regions, flooding in the Ohio River Valley, the primary soft red winter wheat area, and massive snow melt in the Dakotas which could delay spring plantings.

On the day, Cargill Inc bought 2.5 million July on the open. Continental Grain bought one million May and 1.5 million July. FIMAT Futures was also a buyer of the July while LFG was a seller, traders said.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 16,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 12,337 contracts.
